    ".min.js", ".min.css", ".map", ".lock", ".pyc", ".pyo",
    ".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".webp", ".ico", ".pdf",
    ".zip", ".gz", ".tar", ".whl", ".so", ".dylib", ".dll",
)

PY_ROUTE_METHODS = {"get", "post", "put", "delete", "patch", "head", "options", "route"}

_PY_CLASS_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)class\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\b")
_PY_DEF_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(?:async\s+)?def\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\b")
_JS_FUNCTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)"
)
_JS_CLASS_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?class\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)"
)
_JS_CONST_FN_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*=\s*"
    r"(?:async\s*)?(?:\([^)]*\)\s*=>|function\b|\()"
)
_JS_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
    r"""(?:import\s+.*?\s+from\s+|require\s*\(\s*)['"]([^'"]+)['"]"""
)
_JS_ROUTE_RE = re.compile(
    r"""(?:router|app|api)\.(get|post|put|delete|patch)\(\s*['"`]([^'"`]+)"""
)
_MD_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,3})\s+(.+?)\s*$")
_FRONTMATTER_RE = re.compile(r"\A---\s*\n(.*?)\n---\s*\n", re.DOTALL)


def _run_git(root: str, *args: str, timeout: int = 30) -> Optional[str]:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", root, *args],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as ex:
        logger.debug("git %s failed in %s: %s", args, root, ex)
        return None
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return result.stdout


class AtlasIndexer:
    """Build and refresh the atlas database for one project root."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        root: str,
        db_path: str,
        project_name: str = "",
        max_files: int = DEFAULT_MAX_FILES,
        ttl_seconds: int = DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS,
        exclude_paths: Sequence[str] = (),
        ignore_patterns: Any = (),
        codx_path: str = "",
    ):
        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
        self.db_path = db_path
        # Project ``.codx`` folder. The database itself lives in the runtime
        # folder, so the sibling artefacts (``wiki_settings.json``) can no
        # longer be derived from ``db_path`` alone.
        self.codx_path = str(codx_path or "")
        self.project_name = project_name or os.path.basename(self.root)
        self.max_files = max(100, int(max_files or DEFAULT_MAX_FILES))
        # Child projects own their atlas: do not index their files here.
        self.exclude_paths = tuple(
            str(path).replace(os.sep, "/").strip("/")
            for path in (exclude_paths or ())
            if str(path).strip("/")
        )
        # The project's own definition of "project content"
        # (``settings.get_ignore_patterns()``). Accepted as a sequence or as a
        # zero-argument callable so building the atlas facade stays cheap.
        self._ignore_source = ignore_patterns
        self._ignore_cache: Optional[Tuple[str, ...]] = None
        self.ttl_seconds = max(0, int(ttl_seconds or 0))
        self._calls_seen = 0
        self._pending_calls: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        self._pending_edges: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        self._symbol_names: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, str]]] = {}
        self.truncated = False
        self.warnings: List[str] = []
        self._git_top_level: Optional[str] = None
        self._wiki_source_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None

    # ── public entry point ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def ensure(self, force: bool = False) -> AtlasStore:
        """Open the store and make sure it reflects the current working tree."""
        started = time.time()
        store = AtlasStore(self.db_path)
        try:
            paths = store.file_paths()
            index_version = int(store.get_meta("index_version") or 0)
            if paths and index_version != ATLAS_INDEX_VERSION:
                logger.info(
                    "Atlas: index version %s -> %s, rebuilding",
                    index_version,
                    ATLAS_INDEX_VERSION,
                )
                store.reset_schema()
                paths = []
            if force or not paths:
                self._build_full(store, started)
                return store

            checked_at = float(store.get_meta("checked_at") or 0)
            if not force and time.time() - checked_at < self.ttl_seconds:
                return store
            store.set_meta("checked_at", time.time())
            store.conn.commit()

            head = self._git_head()
            indexed_head = str(store.get_meta("commit") or "")
            if head and indexed_head and head != indexed_head:
                logger.info("Atlas: HEAD changed, rebuilding %s", self.root)
                self._build_full(store, started)
                return store

            changed = self._git_changes()
            current = self._list_files()
            if changed is None:
                # No git: compare mtimes with the stored inventory.
                changed = self._mtime_changes(store, current)
            if changed and len(changed) > MAX_INCREMENTAL_FILES:
                logger.info(
                    "Atlas: %d changed files, rebuilding instead of patching",
                    len(changed),
                )
                self._build_full(store, started)
                return store
            if changed:
                self._apply_incremental(store, changed, current)
                self._finish_build(store, started)
            else:
                self._prune_missing(store, current)
                store.set_meta("dirty", False)
                store.set_meta("changed_files", 0)
                store.conn.commit()
            return store
        except Exception:
            store.close()
            raise

    def build(self, force: bool = True) -> AtlasStore:
        """Public alias used by the rebuild endpoint."""
        return self.ensure(force=force)

    # ── full build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _build_full(self, store: AtlasStore, started: float) -> None:
        self.truncated = False
        self.warnings = []
        self._pending_calls = []
        self._pending_edges = []
        self._symbol_names = {}
        self._calls_seen = 0

        paths = self._list_files()
        store.begin_bulk()
        store.clear()
        # Phase 1: create every file node first, so import/doc/test edges can
        # resolve regardless of indexing order.
        for rel_path in paths:
            store.upsert_file_node(
                rel_path,
                os.path.basename(rel_path),
                1,
                self._language(rel_path),
            )
        # Phase 2: parse contents. A single transaction keeps the build fast:
        # committing per file costs a WAL fsync per file.
        for rel_path in paths:
            try:
                self._index_file(store, rel_path, fresh=True)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - one bad file must not kill the index
                logger.warning("Atlas: cannot index %s: %s", rel_path, ex)
                self.warnings.append(f"{rel_path}: {ex}")
        store.conn.commit()
        self._resolve_pending(store)
        store.end_bulk()
        self._finish_build(store, started)

    def _apply_incremental(
        self,
        store: AtlasStore,
        changed: Sequence[str],
        current: Sequence[str],
    ) -> None:
        self._pending_calls = []
        self._pending_edges = []
        self._symbol_names = {}
        self._calls_seen = 0
        for rel_path in changed:
            rel_path = os.path.normpath(rel_path)
            if rel_path not in current:
                store.delete_file(rel_path)
                continue
            store.upsert_file_node(
                rel_path,
                os.path.basename(rel_path),
                1,
                self._language(rel_path),
            )
            try:
                self._index_file(store, rel_path, fresh=False)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover
                logger.exception("Atlas: cannot update %s: %s", rel_path, ex)
                self.warnings.append(f"{rel_path}: {ex}")
        store.conn.commit()
        self._resolve_pending(store)
        self._prune_missing(store, current)
        store.set_meta("dirty", bool(self._git_changes()))
        store.set_meta("changed_files", len(changed))

    def _finish_build(self, store: AtlasStore, started: float) -> None:
        stats = store.stats()
        duration = time.time() - started
        store.set_meta("index_version", ATLAS_INDEX_VERSION)
        store.set_meta("built_at", time.time())
        store.set_meta("checked_at", time.time())
        store.set_meta("duration_seconds", round(duration, 3))
        store.set_meta("commit", self._git_head() or "")
        store.set_meta("dirty", bool(self._git_changes()))
        store.set_meta("file_count", stats["files"])
        store.set_meta("truncated", self.truncated)
        store.set_meta("warnings", self.warnings[-20:])
        store.set_meta("project", self.project_name)
        store.conn.commit()

    # ── file discovery ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _list_files(self) -> List[str]:
        paths: List[str] = []
        tracked = _run_git(self.root, "ls-files", "-z")
        if tracked is not None:
            paths = [self._relative_to_root(item) for item in tracked.split("\0") if item]
            others = _run_git(self.root, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z")
            if others:
                paths.extend(
                    self._relative_to_root(item) for item in others.split("\0") if item
                )
        if not paths:
            paths = self._walk_files()

        candidates = []
        for raw in paths:
            rel_path = os.path.normpath(raw or "")
            if not rel_path or rel_path.startswith("..") or not self._is_candidate(rel_path):
                continue
            candidates.append(rel_path)

        candidates = sorted(
            set(candidates),
            key=lambda path: (self._role_priority(path), path),
        )
        if len(candidates) > self.max_files:
            self.truncated = True
            candidates = candidates[: self.max_files]
        return candidates

    def _relative_to_root(self, raw_path: str) -> str:
        """Normalize a git path to a path relative to this project root."""
        candidate = raw_path
        if not os.path.isabs(candidate):
            direct = os.path.join(self.root, candidate)
            if os.path.exists(direct):
                return os.path.relpath(direct, self.root)
            if self._git_top_level is None:
                self._git_top_level = (
                    _run_git(self.root, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel") or ""
                ).strip()
            if self._git_top_level:
                candidate = os.path.join(self._git_top_level, candidate)
        return os.path.relpath(candidate, self.root)

    def _walk_files(self) -> List[str]:
        found = []
        for current_root, dirs, files in os.walk(self.root):
            dirs[:] = [
                directory for directory in dirs
                if directory not in IGNORED_PARTS
                and not directory.startswith(".")
                and not self._ignored(
                    os.path.relpath(
                        os.path.join(current_root, directory), self.root
                    )
                )
            ]
            for file_name in files:
                abs_path = os.path.join(current_root, file_name)
                found.append(os.path.relpath(abs_path, self.root))
        return found

    def _ignore_patterns(self) -> Tuple[str, ...]:
        """
        Resolve the project ignore patterns once per indexer.

        ``CODXJuniorSettings.get_ignore_patterns()`` is the single definition of
        "what is project content" in codx-junior: ``.git``, ``.codx``,
        ``node_modules``, the wiki folder, ``knowledge_file_ignore`` and the
        child projects. The knowledge base and the file tools already honor it,
        so the atlas must not disagree about the boundaries of the project.

        It is resolved lazily (and cached) because it is only needed while
        building an index, never to open an existing one.
        """
        if self._ignore_cache is None:
            source = self._ignore_source
            try:
                values = source() if callable(source) else source
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                logger.warning("Atlas: cannot resolve ignore patterns: %s", ex)
                values = ()
            self._ignore_cache = tuple(
                str(value).replace(os.sep, "/").strip()
                for value in (values or ())
                if str(value).strip()
            )
        return self._ignore_cache

    def _ignored(self, rel_path: str) -> bool:
        """True when ``rel_path`` is excluded by the project ignore patterns."""
        patterns = self._ignore_patterns()
        if not patterns:
            return False
        posix_path = rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        abs_path = os.path.join(self.root, rel_path).replace(os.sep, "/")
        for pattern in patterns:
            if pattern.startswith("/") or os.path.isabs(pattern):
                base = pattern.rstrip("/")
                if (
                    abs_path == base
                    or abs_path.startswith(f"{base}/")
                    or base in abs_path
                ):
                    return True
                continue
            # Same substring semantics as
            # ``CODXJuniorSettings.is_valid_project_file`` so both layers agree.
            if pattern in posix_path:
                return True
        return False

    def _is_candidate(self, rel_path: str) -> bool:
        if self.exclude_paths:
            posix_path = rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
            if any(
                posix_path == prefix or posix_path.startswith(f"{prefix}/")
                for prefix in self.exclude_paths
            ):
                return False
        if self._ignored(rel_path):
            return False
        parts = rel_path.split(os.sep)
        if any(part in IGNORED_PARTS for part in parts):
            return False
        name = parts[-1]
        if name in IGNORED_NAMES or name.startswith("."):
            return False
        lower = name.lower()
        if lower.endswith(IGNORED_SUFFIXES):
            return False
        ext = os.path.splitext(lower)[1]
        if ext not in INDEXED_EXT:
            return False
        try:
            abs_path = os.path.join(self.root, rel_path)
            if os.path.getsize(abs_path) > MAX_FILE_BYTES:
                return False
        except OSError:
            return False
        return True

    def _role_priority(self, rel_path: str) -> int:
        role = self._role(rel_path)
        return {"source": 0, "test": 1, "doc": 2, "config": 3}.get(role, 4)

    # ── one file ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _index_file(self, store: AtlasStore, rel_path: str, fresh: bool = False) -> None:
        abs_path = os.path.join(self.root, rel_path)
        text = self._read_text(abs_path)
        if text is None:
            store.delete_file(rel_path)
            return
        lines = text.splitlines()
        language = self._language(rel_path)
        role = self._role(rel_path)
        tree = None
        if language == "python":
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(text, filename=rel_path)
            except SyntaxError:
                tree = None
        summary = self._summary(rel_path, text, language, tree)
        stat = os.stat(abs_path)
        record = {
            "path": rel_path,
            "lang": language,
            "role": role,
            "domain": self._domain(rel_path),
            "size": stat.st_size,
            "mtime": stat.st_mtime,
            "sha1": hashlib.sha1(text.encode("utf-8", "ignore")).hexdigest(),
            "summary": summary,
            "indexed_at": time.time(),
        }
        store.upsert_file(record)
        store.upsert_file_node(rel_path, os.path.basename(rel_path), len(lines), language)

        nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        edges: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        if language == "python":
            nodes, edges = self._parse_python(rel_path, text, lines, tree)
        elif language in ("javascript", "typescript", "vue"):
            nodes, edges = self._parse_javascript(rel_path, text, lines, language)
        elif language == "markdown":
            nodes, edges = self._parse_markdown(rel_path, text, lines)

        # Every symbol is contained by its file node.
        for node in nodes:
            if node.get("kind") in ("symbol", "route", "doc"):
                edges.append({
                    "src_key": f"file:{rel_path}",
                    "dst_key": node["key"],
                    "kind": "contains",
                    "confidence": 1.0,
                    "line": node.get("start_line") or 1,
                })

        fts_name = " ".join(
            [rel_path, summary]
            + [node.get("name", "") for node in nodes if node.get("name")]
        )
        body = text[:MAX_BODY_CHARS]
        store.replace_symbols(
            rel_path, nodes, edges, body, fts_name, fresh=fresh
        )

        # Deferred cross-file edges.
        self._pending_edges.extend(self._deferred_edges(rel_path, role, edges))
        for node in nodes:
            if node.get("kind") == "symbol":
                self._symbol_names.setdefault(node["name"], []).append({
                    "key": node["key"],
                    "path": rel_path,
                })
        if language == "python":
            self._collect_python_calls(rel_path, text, tree)

    # ── Python ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _parse_python(
        self,
        rel_path: str,
        text: str,
        lines: Sequence[str],
        tree: Optional[ast.AST] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
        nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        edges: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        if tree is None:
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(text, filename=rel_path)
            except SyntaxError:
                return nodes, edges

        def visit(node: ast.AST, parents: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
            for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
                if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
                    kind = "class" if isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef) else "function"
                    qualname = ".".join([name for _, name in parents] + [child.name])
                    key = f"symbol:{rel_path}:{qualname}"
                    start = int(getattr(child, "lineno", 1) or 1)
                    end = int(getattr(child, "end_lineno", start) or start)
                    parent_key = parents[-1][0] if parents else ""
                    nodes.append({
                        "key": key,
                        "kind": "symbol",
                        "name": child.name,
                        "qualname": qualname,
                        "start_line": start,
                        "end_line": end,
                        "parent_key": parent_key,
                        "lang": "python",
                        "meta": {
                            "python_kind": kind,
                            "decorators": [
                                self._safe_unparse(decorator)
                                for decorator in getattr(child, "decorator_list", [])
                            ],
                        },
                    })
                    if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                        route = self._python_route(child, rel_path, start)
                        if route:
                            route_key = f"route:{rel_path}:{route['name']}:{start}"
                            nodes.append({
                                "key": route_key,
                                "kind": "route",
                                "name": route["name"],
                                "qualname": route["name"],
                                "start_line": start,
                                "end_line": start,
                                "parent_key": "",
                                "lang": "python",
                                "meta": {"framework": "python"},
                            })
                            edges.append({
                                "src_key": route_key,
                                "dst_key": key,
                                "kind": "handles",
                                "confidence": 1.0,
                                "line": start,
                            })
                    visit(child, parents + [(key, child.name)])
                else:
                    visit(child, parents)

        visit(tree, [])

        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                for alias in node.names:
                    target = self._resolve_py_module(alias.name)
                    if target:
                        edges.append(self._import_edge(rel_path, target, getattr(node, "lineno", 0)))
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                target = self._resolve_py_from(rel_path, node)
                if target:
                    edges.append(self._import_edge(rel_path, target, getattr(node, "lineno", 0)))
        return nodes, edges

    def _collect_python_calls(
        self, rel_path: str, text: str, tree: Optional[ast.AST] = None
    ) -> None:
        if self._calls_seen >= MAX_CALL_EDGES:
            return
        if tree is None:
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(text, filename=rel_path)
            except SyntaxError:
                return

        def direct_calls(node: ast.AST, caller_qualname: str) -> None:
            """Collect calls in one function body, not in nested functions."""
            for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
                if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
                    continue
                if isinstance(child, ast.Call):
                    name = self._call_name(child.func)
                    if name:
                        self._pending_calls.append({
                            "path": rel_path,
                            "caller_qualname": caller_qualname,
                            "name": name,
                            "line": int(getattr(child, "lineno", 0) or 0),
                        })
                        self._calls_seen += 1
                        if self._calls_seen >= MAX_CALL_EDGES:
                            return
                direct_calls(child, caller_qualname)

        def visit(node: ast.AST, parents: List[str]) -> None:
            for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
                if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                    qualname = ".".join(parents + [child.name])
                    direct_calls(child, qualname)
                    visit(child, parents + [child.name])
                elif isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
                    visit(child, parents + [child.name])
                else:
                    visit(child, parents)

        visit(tree, [])

    @staticmethod
    def _call_name(func: ast.AST) -> str:
        if isinstance(func, ast.Name):
            return func.id
        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
            return func.attr
        return ""

    def _python_route(self, node: ast.AST, rel_path: str, line: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
        for decorator in getattr(node, "decorator_list", []):
            target = decorator.func if isinstance(decorator, ast.Call) else decorator
            name = self._safe_unparse(target)
            method = name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower()
            if method not in PY_ROUTE_METHODS:
                continue
            route_path = ""
            if isinstance(decorator, ast.Call) and decorator.args:
                first = decorator.args[0]
                if isinstance(first, ast.Constant) and isinstance(first.value, str):
                    route_path = first.value
            if not route_path:
                continue
            http_method = "ROUTE" if method == "route" else method.upper()
            return {"name": f"{http_method} {route_path}"}
        return None

    def _resolve_py_module(self, module: str) -> Optional[str]:
        parts = module.replace(".", "/")
        for candidate in (f"{parts}.py", f"{parts}/__init__.py"):
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, candidate)):
                return candidate
        return None

    def _resolve_py_from(self, rel_path: str, node: ast.ImportFrom) -> Optional[str]:
        if not node.module and not node.level:
            return None
        if node.level:
            base = os.path.dirname(rel_path)
            for _ in range(max(0, int(node.level) - 1)):
                base = os.path.dirname(base)
            module = (node.module or "").replace(".", "/")
            candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, module)) if module else base
            for path in (f"{candidate}.py", os.path.join(candidate, "__init__.py")):
                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(self.root, path), self.root)
                if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, rel)):
                    return rel
            return None
        return self._resolve_py_module(node.module or "")

    @staticmethod
    def _safe_unparse(node: ast.AST) -> str:
        try:
            return ast.unparse(node)
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - old Python
            return type(node).__name__

    # ── JavaScript / TypeScript / Vue ───────────────────────────────────────

    def _parse_javascript(
        self,
        rel_path: str,
        text: str,
        lines: Sequence[str],
        language: str,
    ) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
        nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        edges: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        offset = 0
        script = text
        if language == "vue":
            match = re.search(r"<script[^>]*>(.*?)</script>", text, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
            if match:
                script = match.group(1)
                offset = text[: match.start(1)].count("\n")
            else:
                script = ""
        for index, line in enumerate(script.splitlines(), 1):
            if line.lstrip().startswith(("//", "*", "/*")):
                continue
            match = (
                _JS_CLASS_RE.match(line)
                or _JS_FUNCTION_RE.match(line)
                or _JS_CONST_FN_RE.match(line)
            )
            if not match:
                continue
            name = match.group(1)
            start = index + offset
            key = f"symbol:{rel_path}:{name}"
            if any(node["key"] == key for node in nodes):
                continue
            nodes.append({
                "key": key,
                "kind": "symbol",
                "name": name,
                "qualname": name,
                "start_line": start,
                "end_line": start,
                "parent_key": "",
                "lang": language,
                "meta": {"javascript_kind": "class" if _JS_CLASS_RE.match(line) else "function"},
            })
        for match in _JS_ROUTE_RE.finditer(script):
            method = match.group(1).upper()
            route_path = match.group(2)
            line = script[: match.start()].count("\n") + 1 + offset
            name = f"{method} {route_path}"
            nodes.append({
                "key": f"route:{rel_path}:{name}:{line}",
                "kind": "route",
                "name": name,
                "qualname": name,
                "start_line": line,
                "end_line": line,
                "parent_key": "",
                "lang": language,
                "meta": {"framework": "javascript"},
            })
        for match in _JS_IMPORT_RE.finditer(script):
            target = self._resolve_js_import(rel_path, match.group(1))
            if target:
                line = script[: match.start()].count("\n") + 1 + offset
                edges.append(self._import_edge(rel_path, target, line))
        if language == "vue":
            # The component itself is a useful landmark.
            component = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(rel_path))[0]
            key = f"symbol:{rel_path}:{component}"
            if not any(node["key"] == key for node in nodes):
                nodes.append({
                    "key": key,
                    "kind": "symbol",
                    "name": component,
                    "qualname": component,
                    "start_line": 1,
                    "end_line": max(1, len(lines)),
                    "parent_key": "",
                    "lang": "vue",
                    "meta": {"javascript_kind": "component"},
                })
        return nodes, edges

    def _resolve_js_import(self, rel_path: str, specifier: str) -> Optional[str]:
        if not specifier.startswith("."):
            if specifier.startswith("@/"):
                specifier = "./" + specifier[2:]
            elif specifier.startswith("~/"):
                specifier = "./" + specifier[2:]
            else:
                return None
        base = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(rel_path), specifier))
        candidates = [
            base,
            f"{base}.ts",
            f"{base}.tsx",
            f"{base}.js",
            f"{base}.jsx",
            f"{base}.vue",
            f"{base}.mjs",
            f"{base}.cjs",
            os.path.join(base, "index.ts"),
            os.path.join(base, "index.tsx"),
            os.path.join(base, "index.js"),
            os.path.join(base, "index.vue"),
        ]
        for candidate in candidates:
            if candidate.startswith(".."):
                continue
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, candidate)):
                return candidate
        return None

    # ── Markdown ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _parse_markdown(
        self, rel_path: str, text: str, lines: Sequence[str]
    ) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
        nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        edges: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        frontmatter = self._frontmatter(text)
        title = str(frontmatter.get("title") or "").strip()
        if not title:
            for line in lines[:40]:
                if line.startswith("# "):
                    title = line[2:].strip()
                    break
        title = title or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(rel_path))[0]
        page_key = f"doc:{rel_path}:page"
        nodes.append({
            "key": page_key,
            "kind": "doc",
            "name": title,
            "qualname": title,
            "start_line": 1,
            "end_line": max(1, len(lines)),
            "parent_key": "",
            "lang": "markdown",
            "meta": {
                "description": frontmatter.get("description") or "",
                "tags": frontmatter.get("tags") or [],
            },
        })
        headings = []
        for index, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            match = _MD_HEADING_RE.match(line)
            if match:
                headings.append((index, match.group(2).strip()))
        for position, (line, heading) in enumerate(headings):
            end = headings[position + 1][0] - 1 if position + 1 < len(headings) else len(lines)
            nodes.append({
                "key": f"doc:{rel_path}:{heading}:{line}",
                "kind": "doc",
                "name": heading,
                "qualname": heading,
                "start_line": line,
                "end_line": max(line, end),
                "parent_key": page_key,
                "lang": "markdown",
                "meta": {"heading": True},
            })
        sources = frontmatter.get("source") or frontmatter.get("sources") or frontmatter.get("file")
        if not sources:
            sources = self._wiki_sources().get(rel_path)
        if isinstance(sources, str):
            sources = [sources]
        for source in sources if isinstance(sources, list) else []:
            target = self._resolve_doc_source(rel_path, str(source))
            if target:
                edges.append({
                    "src_key": page_key,
                    "dst_key": f"file:{target}",
                    "kind": "documents",
                    "confidence": 1.0,
                    "line": 1,
                })
        return nodes, edges

    def _wiki_settings_path(self) -> str:
        """
        Locate ``wiki_settings.json``.

        It is a generated cache: the runtime folder holds the current one and
        ``<codx_path>`` the one written by older releases, so both are tried
        before giving up.
        """
        candidates: List[str] = []
        if self.codx_path:
            candidates.append(runtime_file(self.codx_path, WIKI_SETTINGS_FILE))
            candidates.append(os.path.join(self.codx_path, WIKI_SETTINGS_FILE))
        candidates.append(
            os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(self.db_path)), WIKI_SETTINGS_FILE)
        )
        for path in candidates:
            if os.path.isfile(path):
                return path
        return ""

    def _wiki_sources(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """Map generated wiki pages to source files (legacy wiki_settings)."""
        if self._wiki_source_map is not None:
            return self._wiki_source_map
        self._wiki_source_map = {}
        settings_path = self._wiki_settings_path()
        if not settings_path:
            return self._wiki_source_map
        try:
            with open(settings_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                data = json.load(handle)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return self._wiki_source_map

        def visit(categories):
            for category in categories or []:
                for entry in category.get("files") or []:
                    source = str(entry.get("path") or "").lstrip("/")
                    wiki_file = str(entry.get("wiki_file") or "")
                    if not source or not wiki_file:
                        continue
                    try:
                        rel_wiki = os.path.relpath(wiki_file, self.root).replace(os.sep, "/")
                    except ValueError:
                        continue
                    if rel_wiki.startswith(".."):
                        continue
                    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, rel_wiki)) and os.path.isfile(
                        os.path.join(self.root, source)
                    ):
                        self._wiki_source_map[rel_wiki] = source
                visit(category.get("children") or [])

        visit(data.get("categories") or [])
        return self._wiki_source_map

    def _resolve_doc_source(self, rel_path: str, source: str) -> Optional[str]:
        source = source.strip().strip("`'\"")
        if not source:
            return None
        candidates = [
            os.path.normpath(source),
            os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(rel_path), source)),
        ]
        for candidate in candidates:
            if candidate.startswith(".."):
                continue
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, candidate)):
                return candidate
        return None

    @staticmethod
    def _frontmatter(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        match = _FRONTMATTER_RE.match(text)
        if not match:
            return {}
        data: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for raw_line in match.group(1).splitlines():
            line = raw_line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#") or ":" not in line:
                continue
            key, value = line.split(":", 1)
            key = key.strip().lower()
            value = value.strip().strip("'\"")
            if value.startswith("[") and value.endswith("]"):
                value = [
                    item.strip().strip("'\"")
                    for item in value[1:-1].split(",")
                    if item.strip()
                ]
            data[key] = value
        return data

    # ── shared helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _import_edge(rel_path: str, target: str, line: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "src_key": f"file:{rel_path}",
            "dst_key": f"file:{target}",
            "kind": "imports",
            "confidence": 1.0,
            "line": int(line or 0),
        }

    def _deferred_edges(
        self, rel_path: str, role: str, edges: Sequence[Dict[str, Any]]
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        deferred = []
        if role == "test":
            for edge in edges:
                if edge.get("kind") == "imports":
                    deferred.append({
                        "src_key": f"file:{rel_path}",
                        "dst_key": edge["dst_key"],
                        "kind": "tests",
                        "confidence": 0.8,
                        "line": edge.get("line") or 0,
                    })
        return deferred

    def _resolve_pending(self, store: AtlasStore) -> None:
        by_name: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, str]]] = {}
        for row in store.conn.execute(
            "SELECT key, name, path FROM nodes WHERE kind = 'symbol'"
        ):
            by_name.setdefault(row["name"], []).append({
                "key": row["key"],
                "path": row["path"],
            })
        edges: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for call in self._pending_calls:
            candidates = by_name.get(call["name"]) or []
            if len(candidates) == 1:
                target = candidates[0]
            else:
                same_file = [item for item in candidates if item["path"] == call["path"]]
                if len(same_file) != 1:
                    continue
                target = same_file[0]
            edges.append({
                "src_key": f"symbol:{call['path']}:{call['caller_qualname']}"
                if call.get("caller_qualname")
                else f"file:{call['path']}",
                "dst_key": target["key"],
                "kind": "calls",
                "confidence": 0.7,
                "line": call.get("line") or 0,
            })
        edges.extend(self._pending_edges)
        if edges:
            store.add_edges(edges)
        self._pending_calls = []
        self._pending_edges = []

    def _mtime_changes(self, store: AtlasStore, current: Sequence[str]) -> List[str]:
        known = {row["path"]: row for row in store.files()}
        changed = []
        for rel_path in current:
            record = known.get(rel_path)
            try:
                mtime = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(self.root, rel_path))
            except OSError:
                continue
            if not record or float(record.get("mtime") or 0) < mtime:
                changed.append(rel_path)
        changed.extend(path for path in known if path not in current)
        return changed

    def _git_head(self) -> str:
        output = _run_git(self.root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
        return (output or "").strip()

    def _git_changes(self) -> Optional[List[str]]:
        output = _run_git(self.root, "status", "--porcelain")
        if output is None:
            return None
        changed: Set[str] = set()
        for line in output.splitlines():
            if len(line) < 4:
                continue
            status = line[:2]
            payload = line[3:].strip()
            if " -> " in payload:
                old, new = payload.split(" -> ", 1)
                changed.add(self._relative_to_root(old.strip().strip('"')))
                changed.add(self._relative_to_root(new.strip().strip('"')))
            elif payload:
                changed.add(self._relative_to_root(payload.strip('"')))
        return sorted(
            path for path in changed
            if path and self._is_candidate(path)
        )

    def _prune_missing(self, store: AtlasStore, current: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        current_set = set(current)
        for path in store.file_paths():
            if path not in current_set:
                store.delete_file(path)

    def _read_text(self, abs_path: str) -> Optional[str]:
        try:
            if os.path.getsize(abs_path) > MAX_FILE_BYTES:
                return None
            with open(abs_path, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except OSError:
            return None
        if b"\x00" in raw:
            return None
        return raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")

    @staticmethod
    def _language(rel_path: str) -> str:
        ext = os.path.splitext(rel_path)[1].lower()
        return {
            ".py": "python",
            ".ts": "typescript",
            ".tsx": "typescript",
            ".js": "javascript",
            ".jsx": "javascript",
            ".mjs": "javascript",
            ".cjs": "javascript",
            ".vue": "vue",
            ".md": "markdown",
            ".mdx": "markdown",
            ".rst": "markdown",
            ".json": "json",
            ".yaml": "yaml",
            ".yml": "yaml",
            ".toml": "toml",
            ".sh": "shell",
            ".bash": "shell",
            ".sql": "sql",
        }.get(ext, ext.lstrip(".") or "text")

    @staticmethod
    def _role(rel_path: str) -> str:
        parts = [part.lower() for part in rel_path.split(os.sep)]
        name = parts[-1]
        if (
            any(part in {"test", "tests", "__tests__", "spec", "e2e"} for part in parts[:-1])
            or name.startswith("test_")
            or ".test." in name
            or ".spec." in name
        ):
            return "test"
        ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1]
        if ext in DOC_EXT or name.startswith("readme"):
            return "doc"
        if ext in CONFIG_EXT or name in {
            "Dockerfile", "docker-compose.yml", "docker-compose.yaml",
            "Makefile", "Procfile",
        }:
            return "config"
        return "source"

    @staticmethod
    def _domain(rel_path: str) -> str:
        parts = rel_path.split(os.sep)
        if len(parts) == 1:
            return "root"
        if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[0] == "api" and parts[1] == "codx":
            return "api"
        return parts[0]

    def _summary(
        self, rel_path: str, text: str, language: str, tree: Optional[ast.AST] = None
    ) -> str:
        if language == "markdown":
            frontmatter = self._frontmatter(text)
            summary = str(frontmatter.get("description") or "").strip()
            if summary:
                return summary[:300]
            for line in text.splitlines():
                stripped = line.strip()
                if stripped and not stripped.startswith(("#", "---", "```")):
                    return stripped[:300]
            return ""
        if language == "python":
            docstring = ast.get_docstring(tree) if tree is not None else None
            if docstring:
                return " ".join(docstring.split())[:300]
        for line in text.splitlines()[:40]:
            stripped = line.strip()
            if stripped.startswith(("//", "#", "/*", "*")):
                return stripped.lstrip("/*# ").strip()[:300]
        return ""


def index_project(
    root: str,
    db_path: str,
    project_name: str = "",
    force: bool = False,
    max_files: int = DEFAULT_MAX_FILES,
    ttl_seconds: int = DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS,
    exclude_paths: Sequence[str] = (),
    ignore_patterns: Any = (),
    codx_path: str = "",
) -> AtlasStore:
    """Convenience entry point used by tests and non-settings callers."""
    return AtlasIndexer(
        root=root,
        codx_path=codx_path,
        db_path=db_path,
        project_name=project_name,
        max_files=max_files,
        ttl_seconds=ttl_seconds,
        exclude_paths=exclude_paths,
        ignore_patterns=ignore_patterns,
    ).ensure(force=force)

"""
Ephemeral runtime folders shared by the platform subsystems.

``<project>/.codx`` is *durable* state: project settings, profiles and task
cards a human edits. Everything the platform writes while it runs — locks,
worker heartbeats, atomic temp files and rebuildable caches such as the project
atlas or the dependency graph — must not land there, otherwise the repository
working tree churns on its own and every ``git status`` is noise.

Those files live in a runtime folder instead::

    <CODX_JUNIOR_RUNTIME_PATH>/<project-slug>-<hash>/
        atlas/atlas.db
        board_manager/{worker.json,.state.lock,locks/}
        orchestration/{worker.json,locks/}
        dependency_graph.json
        domain_map.json
        project_summary.md
        wiki_settings.json

The folder is expendable: removing it only costs a rebuild. Its location is
``CODX_JUNIOR_RUNTIME_PATH`` (default ``<tmp>/codx-junior-runtime``, so ``/tmp``
on Linux) because nothing there has to survive a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os

from codx.junior.globals import RUNTIME_FOLDER

#: Generated wiki category index (source file -> wiki page mapping).
WIKI_SETTINGS_FILE = "wiki_settings.json"

def project_runtime_dir(codx_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Return the runtime folder of the project owning ``codx_path``.

    The name is human readable (project folder name plus a short hash of the
    absolute ``codx_path``) so two projects sharing a folder name never collide.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> project_runtime_dir("/projects/app/.codx")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e'
    """
    absolute = os.path.abspath(str(codx_path or "."))
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(absolute)) or "project"
    safe = "".join(char if char.isalnum() or char in "-_." else "-" for char in name)
    digest = hashlib.sha1(absolute.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]
    return os.path.join(RUNTIME_FOLDER, f"{safe}-{digest}")


def runtime_dir(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return (creating it) a folder inside the project's runtime folder.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> runtime_dir("/projects/app/.codx", "board_manager")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e/board_manager'
    """
    path = os.path.join(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), *[p for p in parts if p])
    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def runtime_file(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return a file path inside the project's runtime folder.

    The parent folder is created when ``parts`` has more than one element, so
    callers can hand the path straight to ``open(..., "a")`` or to a lock
    helper without extra bookkeeping.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> runtime_file("/projects/app/.codx", "atlas", "atlas.db")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e/atlas/atlas.db'
    """
    parts = [p for p in parts if p]
    path = os.path.join(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), *parts)
    if len(parts) > 1:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    else:
        os.makedirs(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), exist_ok=True)
    return path

Ephemeral runtime folders shared by the platform subsystems.

``<project>/.codx`` is *durable* state: project settings, profiles and task
cards a human edits. Everything the platform writes while it runs — locks,
worker heartbeats, atomic temp files and rebuildable caches such as the project
atlas or the dependency graph — must not land there, otherwise the repository
working tree churns on its own and every ``git status`` is noise.

Those files live in a runtime folder instead::

    <CODX_JUNIOR_RUNTIME_PATH>/<project-slug>-<hash>/
        atlas/atlas.db
        board_manager/{worker.json,.state.lock,locks/}
        orchestration/{worker.json,locks/}
        dependency_graph.json
        domain_map.json
        project_summary.md
        wiki_settings.json

The folder is expendable: removing it only costs a rebuild. Its location is
``CODX_JUNIOR_RUNTIME_PATH`` (default ``<tmp>/codx-junior-runtime``, so ``/tmp``
on Linux) because nothing there has to survive a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os

from codx.junior.globals import RUNTIME_FOLDER

#: Generated wiki category index (source file -> wiki page mapping).
WIKI_SETTINGS_FILE = "wiki_settings.json"


def project_runtime_dir(codx_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Return the runtime folder of the project owning ``codx_path``.

    The name is human readable (project folder name plus a short hash of the
    absolute ``codx_path``) so two projects sharing a folder name never collide.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> project_runtime_dir("/projects/app/.codx")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e'
    """
    absolute = os.path.abspath(str(codx_path or "."))
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(absolute)) or "project"
    safe = "".join(char if char.isalnum() or char in "-_." else "-" for char in name)
    digest = hashlib.sha1(absolute.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]
    return os.path.join(RUNTIME_FOLDER, f"{safe}-{digest}")


def runtime_dir(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return (creating it) a folder inside the project's runtime folder.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> runtime_dir("/projects/app/.codx", "board_manager")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e/board_manager'
    """
    path = os.path.join(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), *[p for p in parts if p])
    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def runtime_file(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return a file path inside the project's runtime folder.

    The parent folder is created when ``parts`` has more than one element, so
    callers can hand the path straight to ``open(..., "a")`` or to a lock
    helper without extra bookkeeping.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> runtime_file("/projects/app/.codx", "atlas", "atlas.db")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e/atlas/atlas.db'
    """
    parts = [p for p in parts if p]
    path = os.path.join(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), *parts)
    if len(parts) > 1:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    else:
        os.makedirs(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), exist_ok=True)
    return path

        seen = set()
        for file_path in files or []:
            if not file_path:
                continue
            absolute = os.path.abspath(file_path)
            if absolute in seen:
                continue
            if absolute.startswith(os.path.abspath(self.wiki_path)):
                continue
            if not os.path.isfile(absolute):
                continue
            seen.add(absolute)
            unique_files.append(absolute)

        built = 0
        for file_path in unique_files:
            try:
                document = self.create_wiki_document(
                    source=file_path,
                    update_wiki_conf=False,
                )
                if document:
                    built += 1
            except Exception as ex:
                logger.exception("Cannot update wiki page for %s: %s", file_path, ex)

        self._update_wiki_conf()
        self.event_manager.send_event("wiki_updated", {
            "project": self.settings.project_name,
            "reason": reason,
            "files": len(unique_files),
            "pages": built,
        })
        if unique_files:
            logger.info(
                "Wiki batch updated for %s: %d/%d page(s)",
                self.settings.project_name,
                built,
                len(unique_files),
            )
        return built

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Wiki tree creation
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def create_wiki_tree(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Analyse the repository and ask the AI to build / refresh the category tree.
        The result is persisted via save_wiki_settings and also returned.
        """
        repository_files = self.loader.list_repository_files()
        ignore_patterns = [MKDOCS_YAML_FILE_NAME, self.wiki_path]

        def is_valid_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
            return not any(p in file_path for p in ignore_patterns)

        repository_files = [
            f.replace(self.settings.abs_project_path, '')
            for f in repository_files
            if is_valid_file(f)
        ]

        # Domain hints from dependency graph
        wiki_domains = WikiDomains(settings=self.settings, db=self.db, ai=self._get_ai())
        domain_map = wiki_domains.load_domain_map()
        domain_hints = ""
        if domain_map:
            domain_hints = "<domain_hints>\n"
            for d in domain_map:
                files_sample = ", ".join(d.get("files", [])[:10])
                domain_hints += f"  Domain '{d['name']}' contains: {files_sample}\n"
            domain_hints += "</domain_hints>\n"

        repository_files_str = "\n".join(sorted(repository_files))
        logger.info("Valid wiki files:\n%s", repository_files_str)

        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        user_language = wiki_settings.get("language", "English")
        user_instructions = wiki_settings.get("prompt", "")

        try:
            project_info = profile_text(
                self.profile_manager.read_profile("project"), self.settings
            )
        except Exception:
            project_info = ""

        project_kind, languages = self.site_builder.project_kind()
        try:
            summary_prompt = f"""
            <project_info>
            {project_info}
            </project_info>
            <project_kind>{project_kind}</project_kind>
            <languages>{', '.join(languages)}</languages>
            <project_files>
            {repository_files_str}
            </project_files>
            {domain_hints}
            <wiki_settings>
            {json.dumps(wiki_settings, indent=2)}
            </wiki_settings>
            <wiki_profile>
            {self._get_wiki_profile_text()}
            </wiki_profile>
            <wiki_profile_guard>
            {WIKI_PROFILE_GUARD}
            </wiki_profile_guard>
            <user_instructions>
            {user_instructions}
            </user_instructions>
            <user_language>
            {user_language}
            </user_language>

            Design the navigation of a modern documentation site for this project.
            Think like a senior engineer writing the docs a new teammate needs on day one:
            onboarding, architecture, guides, API/reference and operations.

            Return a wiki_settings JSON object with the updated "categories" tree and
            keep the existing top-level keys (language, mode, prompt, assistant).

            Category rules:
            - 5 to 8 top-level categories, each with a clear purpose.
            - Use children only when it genuinely helps (do not create one-child groups).
            - Every category has:
                * "title": unique, 2-4 words, sentence case, in {user_language}
                * "description": one or two sentences explaining what the reader learns
                * "icon": one Font Awesome class, e.g. "fa-solid fa-rocket"
                * "order": integer used to sort the sidebar (10, 20, 30…)
                * "keywords": list of keywords used to match files
                * "children": array of optional child categories
                * "files": list of WikiFile entries (mandatory)
            - WikiFile: {{"name": 2-4 word friendly title in {user_language}, "path": project-relative path}}.
            - Prefer a "Get started" category first, then "Guides", "Architecture",
              "API reference" (or equivalents for the project kind), then operations.
            - For non-code projects, use sections that make sense (e.g. Policies,
              Research, Processes) instead of forcing code structure.
            - Remove files that are no longer present; assign every project file to a category.

            Return ONLY the JSON object. Generated content must be in {user_language}.
            """
            messages = self._ai_chat(prompt=summary_prompt, clean=False)
            new_settings = next(extract_json_blocks(messages[-1].content))
            # Preserve top-level metadata (language, mode, prompt, assistant…)
            for key in ("language", "mode", "prompt", "assistant"):
                if key in wiki_settings and key not in new_settings:
                    new_settings[key] = wiki_settings[key]
            saved = self.save_wiki_settings(new_settings)
            self.build_site()
            return saved

        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception("Error creating wiki tree: %s", ex)
            return {**wiki_settings, "error": str(ex)}

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Document creation
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def create_wiki_document(self, source: str, update_wiki_conf: bool = True) -> Optional[Document]:
        """
        Generate (or refresh) the wiki page for a single source file.

        The generated page uses the modern documentation format: YAML
        frontmatter, a skimmable summary, Mermaid diagrams, runnable examples
        and callout hints. The AI is free to omit a section when it does not
        apply; the page is normalised afterwards so every page always has valid
        metadata and an H1.
        """
        if not self.is_wiki_active:
            logger.debug("Wiki is not active, skipping document creation for %s", source)
            return None

        if source and not os.path.isabs(source):
            source = os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, source)
        source = os.path.abspath(source)

        # Validate source path to prevent malformed filenames
        if not self._is_valid_source_path(source):
            logger.warning("Invalid source path detected: %s", source)
            return None

        file_content = self._read_file(source)
        if not file_content:
            logger.warning("Empty or unreadable file, skipping: %s", source)
            return None

        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        category = self._assign_category_to_file(source, wiki_settings)
        if not category:
            logger.warning(CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE, source)
            return None

        title = category['title']
        keywords = category.get('keywords') or []
        project_name = self.settings.project_name
        wiki_path = category["path"]
        wiki_file_path = self._determine_wiki_file_path(category, source)

        # Validate wiki file path before attempting to read
        if not self._is_valid_wiki_file_path(wiki_file_path):
            logger.error("Invalid wiki file path generated: %s", wiki_file_path)
            return None

        current_wiki_content = ""
        if os.path.isfile(wiki_file_path):
            try:
                with open(wiki_file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                    current_wiki_content = handle.read()
            except OSError as ex:
                logger.debug("Cannot read current wiki page %s: %s", wiki_file_path, ex)

        summary_prompt = self._prepare_summary_prompt(
            current_wiki_content, category, file_content,
            project_name, source, title, keywords, wiki_settings
        )

        messages = self._ai_chat(prompt=summary_prompt)
        page_content = self._normalize_generated_page(
            messages[-1].content,
            category=category,
            source=source,
            wiki_settings=wiki_settings,
        )

        # Append a related-pages / dependency section from the graph. This is
        # deterministic (no AI) and helps the reader jump to connected code.
        try:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if graph.load():
                deps = graph.get_file_deps(source)
                dep_section = self._build_dependency_section(deps, source)
                if dep_section:
                    page_content = f"{page_content.rstrip()}\n\n{dep_section}\n"
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Cannot append dependency section for %s: %s", source, ex)

        logger.info("Writing wiki document to %s", wiki_file_path)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(wiki_file_path), exist_ok=True)
        write_file(wiki_file_path, page_content)

        metadata = {
            "keywords": keywords,
            "category": title,
            "source": source,
            "language": "md",
            "wiki_path": wiki_path,
            "page_path": os.path.splitext(os.path.relpath(wiki_file_path, self.wiki_path))[0].replace(os.sep, "/"),
            "updated_at": int(datetime.datetime.now().timestamp()),
        }

        if update_wiki_conf:
            self._update_wiki_conf()

        return Document(page_content, metadata=metadata)

    def _normalize_generated_page(
        self,
        content: str,
        category: Dict[str, Any],
        source: str,
        wiki_settings: Dict[str, Any],
    ) -> str:
        """
        Make an AI answer a valid, self-describing wiki page.

        * strips accidental outer code fences,
        * guarantees YAML frontmatter (title, description, tags, category, source),
        * guarantees an H1 heading,
        * keeps the body intact.
        """
        text = (content or "").strip()
        if text.startswith("```"):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            if len(lines) >= 2 and lines[-1].strip().startswith("```"):
                text = "\n".join(lines[1:-1]).strip()
        if not text:
            text = f"# {humanize(category.get('title') or source)}"

        frontmatter, body = parse_frontmatter(text)
        body = body.strip()
        title = str(
            frontmatter.get("title")
            or first_heading(body)
            or humanize(os.path.basename(source))
        )
        description = str(
            frontmatter.get("description")
            or first_paragraph(body)
            or f"Documentation for {os.path.relpath(source, self.settings.abs_project_path)}."
        )
        tags = frontmatter.get("tags") or frontmatter.get("keywords") or category.get("keywords") or []
        if isinstance(tags, str):
            tags = [tag.strip() for tag in tags.split(",") if tag.strip()]
        updated = datetime.date.today().isoformat()
        rel_source = os.path.relpath(source, self.settings.abs_project_path).replace(os.sep, "/")
        meta = {
            "title": title,
            "description": description[:300],
            "tags": list(tags),
            "category": category.get("title", ""),
            "source": rel_source,
            "updated": updated,
        }
        if not first_heading(body):
            body = f"# {title}\n\n{body}".strip()
        try:
            header = yaml.safe_dump(meta, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).strip()
        except Exception:
            header = (
                f"title: {json.dumps(title)}\n"
                f"description: {json.dumps(description[:300])}\n"
                f"category: {json.dumps(category.get('title', ''))}\n"
                f"source: {json.dumps(rel_source)}\n"
                f"updated: {updated}"
            )
        return f"---\n{header}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n"

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Category / bulk build
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build_wiki_category(self, path: str) -> None:
        """Build wiki documents for all files in the category at *path*."""
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings(with_files=True)
        categories = self._get_all_categories(wiki_settings["categories"])
        category = next((c for c in categories if c.get("path") == path), None)

        if not category:
            logger.warning("No category found for path: %s", path)
            return

        files = category.get("files", [])
        if not files:
            logger.info("Category '%s' has no files, skipping.", path)
            return

        logger.info("Building wiki category '%s' (%d files)", path, len(files))
        # Warm the repository scan before the worker threads start so parallel
        # page generation does not repeat it.
        self.site_builder.project_kind()
        self.event_manager.send_event(
            "wiki_category_start", {"path": path, "total": len(files)}
        )

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WIKI_BUILD_WORKERS) as executor:
            future_to_file = {
                executor.submit(self.create_wiki_document, f["path"], False): f["path"]
                for f in files
            }
            for future in as_completed(future_to_file):
                file_path = future_to_file[future]
                try:
                    future.result()
                    logger.info("Wiki document built: %s", file_path)
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.exception("Failed to build wiki document for %s: %s", file_path, e)

        self._update_wiki_conf()
        self.event_manager.send_event("wiki_category_done", {"path": path})

    def rebuild_wiki(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild all wiki documents for every category."""
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        categories = self._get_all_categories(wiki_settings["categories"])
        logger.info("Rebuilding entire wiki (%d categories)", len(categories))

        for category in categories:
            self.build_wiki_category(category["path"])

        # Final home + manifest update after all categories are done.
        self.build_wiki_home(self._read_file(self.wiki_home_path) or "")
        self.build_site()
        logger.info("Wiki rebuild complete.")

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Home page
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build_wiki_home(self, markdown_content: str) -> None:
        """
        Regenerate the landing page from the project overview and categories.

        The home page is the front door of the docs site: a short pitch, a
        visual map of the project, quick-start steps and links into the main
        sections. It is regenerated explicitly (settings / refresh), not on
        every single file change.
        """
        self.ensure_wiki_structure()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        user_language = wiki_settings.get("language", "English")
        user_instructions = wiki_settings.get("prompt", "")
        project_kind, languages = self.site_builder.project_kind()

        categories_without_files = [
            {k: v for k, v in cat.items() if k != "files"}
            for cat in self._get_all_categories(wiki_settings["categories"])
        ]

        existing_home = ""
        if os.path.isfile(self.wiki_home_path):
            try:
                with open(self.wiki_home_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                    existing_home = handle.read()
            except OSError:
                existing_home = ""

        if not markdown_content or not markdown_content.strip():
            markdown_content = existing_home or self._default_home_page()
        if not categories_without_files and not existing_home:
            write_file(self.wiki_home_path, self._default_home_page())
            return

        project_name = self.settings.project_name or "Project"
        project_info = ""
        try:
            project_info = profile_text(
                self.profile_manager.read_profile("project"), self.settings
            )
        except Exception:
            project_info = ""

        diagram_rule = (
            "Include a high-level `flowchart TD` Mermaid diagram that shows the "
            "main subsystems and how a request/flow moves through them."
            if project_kind == "code"
            else "Include a Mermaid diagram only if it clarifies the project structure."
        )
        relevance_prompt = f"""
<project_info>
{project_info}
</project_info>
<project_kind>{project_kind}</project_kind>
<languages>{', '.join(languages)}</languages>
<markdown_content>
{markdown_content}
</markdown_content>
<home_page_content>
{existing_home}
</home_page_content>
<categories>
{json.dumps(categories_without_files, indent=2)}
</categories>
<wiki_profile>
{self._get_wiki_profile_text()}
</wiki_profile>
<wiki_profile_guard>
{WIKI_PROFILE_GUARD}
</wiki_profile_guard>
<user_instructions>
{user_instructions}
</user_instructions>

Write the landing page for the {project_name} documentation site in {user_language}.
Make it feel like a modern developer portal: welcoming, skimmable and useful on
first contact. Do not repeat page contents; link to them.

Use this shape:

---
title: "{project_name}"
description: <one sentence>
tags: [overview]
---

# {project_name}

> **<One-line pitch that explains the value.>**

<2 short paragraphs: what it is, who it is for and the problem it solves.>

## What you can do here
- 3-5 outcomes the reader can achieve, each linking to a page as [Title](wiki:path).

## Architecture at a glance
{diagram_rule}
A short explanation of the main parts. Keep it high level.

## Quick start
1. 3-5 concrete first steps with commands in fenced ```bash blocks.

## Explore the docs

## Hints

> [!NOTE]
> Anything to install or configure before starting.

Rules:
- Only use information present in the sources; do not invent features.
- Use links in the form [Page title](wiki:relative/path) when referencing a page.
- Keep it under ~450 words. No raw file paths as headings.
- Return only the final markdown document, without enclosing code fences.
"""
        try:
            messages = self._ai_chat(prompt=relevance_prompt)
            updated_home = messages[-1].content
            frontmatter, body = parse_frontmatter(updated_home)
            if not first_heading(body):
                body = f"# {project_name}\n\n{body}"
            if not frontmatter:
                meta = {
                    "title": project_name,
                    "description": self.site_builder._project_description(project_name),
                    "tags": ["overview"],
                }
                header = yaml.safe_dump(meta, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).strip()
                updated_home = f"---\n{header}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n"
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.wiki_home_path), exist_ok=True)
            write_file(self.wiki_home_path, updated_home)
            logger.info("Wiki home page updated at %s", self.wiki_home_path)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Error updating wiki home page: %s", e)

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Wiki compile / mkdocs
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def compile_wiki(self) -> None:
        """Compile the wiki: refresh the docs manifest and optional static site."""
        site = self.build_site()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        if wiki_settings.get("mode") == "mkdocs":
            self._update_mkdocs(site)

    def _update_wiki_conf(self) -> None:
        """Update the docs manifest and any optional static-site configuration."""
        site = self.build_site()
        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        if wiki_settings.get("mode") == "mkdocs":
            self._update_mkdocs(site)

    def _update_mkdocs(self, site: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
        """
        Keep the MkDocs navigation in sync with the docs-site manifest.

        The old implementation asked the AI to rewrite the nav on every update.
        Navigation is deterministic data, so this is now cheap and correct.
        """
        mkdocs_file_path = Path(self.settings.abs_project_path) / MKDOCS_YAML_FILE_NAME
        site = site or self.site_builder.load() or self.build_site(write=False)
        nav: List[Any] = []
        for section in site.get("navigation", []):
            items = section.get("items", [])
            if not items:
                continue
            entries = []
            for item in items:
                title = item.get("title", "")
                path = item.get("path", "")
                if path:
                    entries.append({title: f"{path}.md"})
            if entries:
                nav.append({section.get("title", "Docs"): entries})

        current: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        if mkdocs_file_path.exists():
            try:
                with open(mkdocs_file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                    loaded = yaml.safe_load(handle)
                if isinstance(loaded, dict):
                    current = loaded
            except Exception as ex:
                logger.warning("Cannot read existing mkdocs.yml: %s", ex)
        current.setdefault("site_name", self.settings.project_name)
        current["nav"] = nav
        try:
            with open(mkdocs_file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                yaml.dump(current, handle, default_flow_style=False, allow_unicode=True)
            logger.info("mkdocs.yml updated at %s", mkdocs_file_path)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Error updating mkdocs.yml: %s", e)

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Dependency graph & domains
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build_dependency_graph(self) -> DependencyGraph:
        """Build and save the project dependency graph."""
        graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
        file_paths = self.loader.list_repository_files()
        ignore_patterns = [self.wiki_path, MKDOCS_YAML_FILE_NAME]
        file_paths = [f for f in file_paths if not any(p in f for p in ignore_patterns)]
        graph.build(file_paths)
        graph.save()
        return graph

    def build_domains(self, graph: DependencyGraph = None) -> List[Dict]:
        """Build domain-based wiki pages."""
        if graph is None:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if not graph.load():
                graph = self.build_dependency_graph()

        source_map = self.db.get_all_sources()
        wiki_domains = WikiDomains(settings=self.settings, db=self.db, ai=self._get_ai())
        domains = wiki_domains.detect_domains(graph=graph, source_map=source_map)

        domains_dir = os.path.join(self.wiki_path, "domains")
        os.makedirs(domains_dir, exist_ok=True)

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WIKI_BUILD_WORKERS) as executor:
            def _build_page(domain: Dict) -> None:
                try:
                    content = wiki_domains.build_domain_page(domain=domain, graph=graph)
                    content = self._ensure_domain_frontmatter(content, domain)
                    page_path = os.path.join(domains_dir, f"{domain['slug']}.md")
                    write_file(page_path, content)
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.exception("Error building domain page for %s: %s", domain.get("name"), ex)

            futures = [executor.submit(_build_page, d) for d in domains]
            for f in as_completed(futures):
                try:
                    f.result()
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.exception("build_domains future error: %s", ex)

        wiki_domains.save_domain_map(domains)
        self.build_site()
        return domains

    def build_wiki_index(self, graph: DependencyGraph = None, domains: List[Dict] = None) -> Dict:
        """Build and index wiki content."""
        if graph is None:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if not graph.load():
                graph = self.build_dependency_graph()
        if domains is None:
            wiki_domains = WikiDomains(settings=self.settings, db=self.db, ai=self._get_ai())
            domains = wiki_domains.load_domain_map()

        wiki_settings = self.load_wiki_settings()
        self.build_site()
        wiki_index = WikiIndex(settings=self.settings, db=self.db)
        index = wiki_index.build(wiki_settings=wiki_settings, domain_map=domains, graph=graph)
        wiki_index.save(index)
        wiki_index.index_to_milvus(index)
        return index

    def _ensure_domain_frontmatter(self, content: str, domain: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Guarantee frontmatter/description on an AI-generated domain page."""
        text = (content or "").strip()
        frontmatter, body = parse_frontmatter(text)
        title = str(frontmatter.get("title") or first_heading(body) or domain.get("name") or "Domain")
        description = str(
            frontmatter.get("description")
            or domain.get("description")
            or first_paragraph(body)
        )
        if not first_heading(body):
            body = f"# {title}\n\n{body}".strip()
        if not frontmatter:
            meta = {
                "title": title,
                "description": description[:300],
                "tags": ["architecture", "domain"],
                "category": "Architecture",
            }
            header = yaml.safe_dump(meta, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).strip()
            return f"---\n{header}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n"
        return f"---\n{yaml.safe_dump(frontmatter, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).strip()}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n"

    def build_module_page(self, file_path: str, graph: DependencyGraph = None) -> str:
        """
        Generate a reference page for one source file.

        The page is written to ``wiki/modules/<slug>.md`` and uses the same
        modern format as the rest of the site: summary, diagram, dependencies,
        example and hints.
        """
        if not os.path.isabs(file_path):
            file_path = os.path.join(self.settings.abs_project_path, file_path)
        file_path = os.path.abspath(file_path)
        if graph is None:
            graph = DependencyGraph(settings=self.settings)
            if not graph.load():
                graph = self.build_dependency_graph()

        deps = graph.get_file_deps(file_path)
        file_content = self._read_file(file_path)
        if not file_content:
